program.notes: let_me_buy (letmebuy.app) — a storefront program: a merchant stands up a store, lists products, and buyers pay in an SPL token by scanning a QR code. ONE PDA per store carries everything: receipts = ['receipts', store_name] (store_name is an instruction ARGUMENT, utf8), and the account holds the products vec, the receipts vec, total_purchases, authority, telegram_channel_id, details and bump. Every one of the eight instructions takes that same account, writable — which is what makes the lifecycle a chain rather than eight unrelated calls, and why product_name is never a seed. Derivation order is trivial (receipts depends on nothing but the store name) and the two associated-token accounts depend only on caller-supplied owner/mint, so nothing here needs a chain read to build. Instruction account lists, in IDL order: initialize(store_name) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer), system_program]; add_product(store_name, name, price:u64) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer), mint, system_program]; make_purchase(store_name, product_name, table_number:u8) = [receipts(w), signer(w,signer), authority(w), mint, sender_token_account(w), recipient_token_account(w), token_program, system_program, associated_token_program] (9); mark_as_delivered(_store_name, receipt_id:u64) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer)]; update_details(store_name, details) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer)]; update_telegram_channel(store_name, telegram_channel_id) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer)]; delete_product(store_name, product_name) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer), system_program]; delete_store(store_name) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer)]. THE JOIN THE IDL LOSES: mark_as_delivered's receipts account declares the seed arg path 'store_name', but that instruction's own args are named '_store_name' and 'receipt_id' — the seed points at an argument that does not exist in its instruction, so an IDL-driven deriver that resolves seed paths by arg name gets nothing for the one seed that selects the store. The recipe here binds by seed VALUE ('store_name' for all eight), and the wire arg for that call stays '_store_name'. SECOND TRAP: in make_purchase the store's `authority` is writable but NOT a signer — the merchant does not co-sign a sale; the program checks it against receipts.authority (6004 InvalidAuthority). The buyer pays from sender_token_account = ATA(signer, token_program, mint) and the store is credited at recipient_token_account = ATA(authority, token_program, mint) — same mint, same token program, different owner; deriving both from the same owner builds a purchase that pays the buyer back. token_program is pinned by the IDL to classic SPL Token (TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA), so both ATAs are classic-Token ATAs and a Token-2022 mint has no path through this program. The currency is fixed per product by add_product's `mint` account (stored with price and decimals in the products vec); a make_purchase whose mint differs fails 6003 InvalidMint. delete_store refuses a store that still has products (6005 StoreNotEmpty) — delete_product first. Other errors: 6001 ProductAlreadyExists, 6002 ProductNotFound, 6006 ProductNameEmpty, 6007 StringTooLong, 6008 VectorLimitReached, 6009 InvalidStoreName. PROVENANCE: the Anchor IDL that states these recipes reached comprehension through the hosted project surface (a third-party mirror), not from the program's own on-chain IDL account, and the seeds were hand-authored into this config from it — so every entry is carried at `manual`, the reviewed-overlay tier, rather than `extracted`. Correctness of the receipts recipe is established separately, by a derived address matching a mainnet account the program owns; that is a chain fact pinned in tests/test_let_me_buy_config.py, and it is evidence, never a tier. No execute intent is wired for this program yet: it is comprehended for DERIVATION only. STORE NAME (observed, not established from source): the program refuses at least one store_name with 6009 InvalidStoreName — 'gecko_coffee' was refused and 'geckocoffee' accepted in the same run — and the two differ by one underscore, which is not enough to state a rule, so none is stated here; see program.arg_constraints.store_name.

store_name.note: OBSERVED, NOT ESTABLISHED FROM SOURCE. The program rejects at least one store_name with error 6009 InvalidStoreName: 'gecko_coffee' was refused (6009, 14,202 CU) and 'geckocoffee' was accepted (8,014 CU) in the same $0 simulation run; 'jonasbar' is a store that exists on mainnet. The two tested names differ by ONE underscore, and two data points cannot tell 'no underscore' apart from 'alphanumeric only' or any other rule, so no rule is stated here. What the artifact does say: every instruction declares store_name as a bare `string` with no length, charset or pattern (an Anchor IDL cannot express one), and length has its OWN code — 6007 StringTooLong — so 6009 is not the too-long answer. Until the check is read from source, treat any store_name outside the accepted list as UNVERIFIED, not as invalid.
